title: Varying Context Window Position: Do SAE Features at the Beginning vs End of a Long Context Differ in Polysemanticity?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if generation-time positions are more polysemantic, the computations most responsible for output are least interpretable -- a practical bottleneck for safety monitoring. The mechanism is plausible but the proposal does not name a specific safety failure prevented by this knowledge.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Per-token activation extraction is documented in TransformerLens and SAELens. Applying a pre-trained SAE (no training needed) and measuring standard metrics at different positions is structured. A beginner with mentor guidance can follow this workflow.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 200 prompts, 5 token positions, three clear metrics per position. Uses pre-trained SAE so no training overhead. Well-bounded comparison with a clear output table/plot.

novelty.reasoning: While SAE feature analysis is well-established and position-dependent behavior in transformers is studied (e.g., attention patterns varying with position), the specific question of whether SAE feature polysemanticity varies systematically with context window position has not been directly published. The shallow alignment literature (Qi et al.) examines token-position effects on alignment but not on SAE feature polysemanticity. This is a genuinely novel angle combining two established research directions.
